reasoning: Both attempts implement every rule correctly and handle untrusted input safely. B wins on comment quality: it has no file header and no repeated NaN note, and its docs stay concise and purposeful. It also has typed failure reasons and a typed result, and it takes the ground height from the Baseplate itself. A's manual AABB overlap test is somewhat more robust than B's physics query, but A's noisier comments and its pointer to another file tip the comparison to B.

criteria.note: Has all five types in BLOCK_TYPES; snapToGrid sets the Y origin to GROUND_Y=0 so cells rest on the Baseplate; checks the 0 to 200 height range, MAX_REACH 24 from the HRP, and an AABB overlap test with OVERLAP_EPSILON so adjacent blocks are allowed; gives short reasons and exposes the snapping.
Checks typeof for both string and Vector3, uses isFiniteVector3 to reject NaN and inf before snapping, and writes the range checks as not(x<=limit) so NaN fails them.

Most comments carry real information (the epsilon is for face-sharing, the normal offset for mouse hits, blocks are never rotated), but the file header and the 'Max distance from...' line on MAX_REACH mostly restate the name.
Has a two-line file header, a long validate doc with an inline usage example, and the NaN point made twice (in isFiniteNumber and in the validate doc).

criteria.criterion: Public functions carry short doc comments
criteria.note: The snapToGrid and validate docs state the return meaning and that the function is idempotent, but the validate doc is long and isValidBlockType has none (acceptable, since it's obvious).

criteria.criterion: No change history or external references
criteria.note: No history, but the comment '(see default.project.json)' points the reader to another file.
A single frozen shared module with no remote or UI; passes all checks; its overlap test works whether or not the parts are in Workspace.

Has the five BlockType values; snapAxis sets the Y origin to getGroundY(baseplate); checks TooLow, TooHigh (200), and TooFar (24 from the HRP); its GetPartBoundsInBox query, shrunk by TOUCH_TOLERANCE, allows adjacent blocks; FailureReason gives short reasons and snapPosition is exposed.
Checks typeof for the string and Vector3 and uses isFiniteVector to reject NaN and inf before snapping or any range check.
Every comment adds information: TOUCH_TOLERANCE explains why the query is shrunk, BlocksFolder states the CanQuery requirement, and the snap doc warns about the side-hit gotcha.
No header or banners and the inline comments are terse; the two doc blocks span four lines but carry content.

criteria.criterion: Public functions carry short doc comments
criteria.note: The snapPosition and validate docs cover the return meaning, the never-errors guarantee, and the raycast nudge, without listing parameters.

criteria.criterion: No change history or external references

NaN-safe comparisons, frozen module and constants
Useful hint about offsetting the hit point by the normal for mouse hits
weaknesses: File header comment and an overlong validate doc
